children: Copper futures rose toward a record in early trading Tuesday as falling inventories and pre-holiday buying signaled tightening supplies in China's physical market, Bloomberg reported.
While some imported copper has arrived in China, much of it has gone directly to fabricators rather than warehouses, keeping spot supplies constrained, Shanghai Metals Market said in a note.
Demand is also enjoying a seasonal boost as some downstream manufacturers stock up ahead of the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays, SMM said.
Additionally, copper cathode inventories in Shanghai fell to 43.9K tons, the lowest since 2023, according to weekly data released by SMM.

"With the dollar having had little influence on recent price action, we see the near-term path for copper as increasingly momentum-led," Sucden Financial said in a note, adding the market could test the $14,750/ton area again, with a sustained move above it signaling stronger upward momentum while renewed selling pressure could prompt traders to lock in gains after the recent rebound.
